real_defects.issue: A semicolon CSV with decimal commas (1,5) was read with the comma stripped as a thousands separator: means 2 and 4 came out as 20 and 40, W1 ten times too large, no warning. Fixed: parseCsv sets decimalComma for ';' and numText reads 1,5 and 1.234,5 as decimals.
Same decimal-comma bug as wasserstein-distance (shared numText): x and y from a ';' CSV read 10x/100x too large. Fixed the same way, including the headerless sniff.
Same decimal-comma bug: a ';' CSV's features were read 10x/100x too large, changing the scaled distances the clusters come from. Fixed the same way.
Same decimal-comma bug: a ';' CSV's features and medians were read 10x/100x too large. Fixed the same way.
parseTable sniffs ';' but cleanNum strips commas: '3,5' read as 35 in every store/region series. Fixed: decimalCommaCell rewrites decimal-comma cells when the delimiter is ';'.
parseSales sniffs ';' but cleanNumber strips commas: a price of 19,99 read as 1999 (100x), so elasticity and markdown prices were fit on wrong prices. Fixed with decimalCommaCell.
parseManifest sniffs ';' but num strips commas: retail 19,99 read as 1999 and 1.249,00 as 1.249, so the pallet's retail total and bid were wrong. Fixed with decimalCommaCell.
